chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: Bunk Johnson forgets the longshoremen's date and flees to Crowley
summary: After Bunk missed a parade date the Irishmen threatened to throw him in the river, so he left for Crowley.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Bunk Johnson booked a date for the longshoremen. And he forgot it! And the parade is waiting to go on, doin' with the umbrellas just like the Blacks. Same thing. And all of them rough Irish chicks is out there in the bar, and the band ain't comin'. And them sumbitches just... Heh...
The sent word, said, "If we catch Bunk Johnson, you tell that son-of-a-bitch we're gonna tie him in a sack and throw him in the river."
Bunk Johnson heard that, and left for Crowley.

Yes. Two hundred miles from there! They said, "They're looking for you, Bunk. Everybody is agitating for you. Bunk, them sumbitches out on the riverfront, all them longshoremen, say, oh, if they get hold

of your ass, that's the end of you." Bunk Johnson got nervous, cut out and went out to Crowley, and went away with the Black Eagle Band, Evan Thomas' band, which was a funky band out there. He went to Crowley...
